title: Capillary-selective vasodilation through myosin inhibition halts ischaemic cascades
source: Nature
abstract: In acute myocardial infarction and acute kidney injury, capillary no-reflow denotes that capillary blood flow is still blocked despite successful arterial reperfusion. This is associated with substantially increased mortality and reinfarction risk; nevertheless, no targeted therapy exists so far1,2. Because capillary no-reflow is driven by smooth muscle myosin-mediated hypercontraction of capillary pericytes, we developed R(+)2501, a myosin-specific and capillary-selective vasodilator. In reperfused animal models of acute myocardial infarction and acute kidney injury, direct in vivo imaging showed that R(+)2501 rapidly restored capillary flow, an effect sustained even after rapid drug clearance. Ex vivo experiments confirmed reversal of pericyte constriction directly. Restoration of capillary blood flow, together with clearance of trapped neutrophils, linked resolution of capillary no-reflow to attenuation of an early driver of reperfusion injury. R(+)2501 enhanced capillary perfusion while preserving coronary autoregulation and systemic haemodynamics, and markedly improved survival during acute reperfusion. We further found that acute myocardial infarction induced renal capillary no-reflow, which was reversed by R(+)2501, suggesting that capillary no-reflow contributes to the pathophysiology of cardiorenal syndrome type I. These findings establish pericyte-targeted smooth muscle myosin inhibition as a therapeutic strategy to restore microvascular perfusion and halt the ischaemic cascade across organs, while defining a specific physiological role for capillaries and pericytes in circulatory regulation.

title: Targeted stimulation of motor cortex ensembles drives learned movements
source: Nature
abstract: During the execution of learned motor skills, the neural population in layer 2/3 (L2/3) of primary motor cortex (M1) expresses a reproducible spatiotemporal activity pattern1. It is debated whether M1 actively participates in generating this learned pattern and whether this pattern causally drives the learned movement2,3,4,5. Here we combined in vivo two-photon calcium imaging and holographic optogenetic stimulation of functionally defined M1 L2/3 ensembles in mice performing a skilled lever-pressing task. Brief synchronous stimulation of about 20 neurons whose activity onset precedes voluntary movement onset induced movements resembling the learned movement, while producing activity patterns in other M1 neurons resembling the learned activity. Moreover, trial-by-trial variability of optogenetically triggered population activity correlated with variability in the induced movements. These variabilities were predicted by the initial state of M1 activity preceding stimulation. In some trials, stimulation induced the learned activity without inducing movements, indicating that the learned activity is not simply a reflection of movements but can arise internally. Stimulation failed to generate movements or learned activity in task-disengaged mice. Stimulation of neurons whose activity followed movement onsets failed to induce the learned movement in task-engaged mice. Together, the learned activity in M1 L2/3 can be generated when M1 is prepared at the optimal initial state and receives precise triggering inputs, supporting the active role of M1 in generating learned activity and learned movements.

title: Computational design of metalloproteases
source: Nature
abstract: De novo design of enzymes that cleave amide bonds represents a major challenge1,2. Here we use RFdiffusion methods3,4 to de novo design proteins with water-activating zinc-based active sites adjacent to a peptide substrate binding pocket. Of 135 designs tested, 36% catalyse cleavage of their cognate peptide substrates at the targeted scissile bond. The best design accelerates peptide-bond hydrolysis by more than 108-fold relative to the uncatalysed reaction; four substitutions increase this acceleration to more than 1010-fold by improving active-site preorganization5. We use this approach to design metalloproteases that selectively cleave the human disease-associated proteins TDP-43, amyloid-β and serum amyloid A, with rate enhancements of up to 109-fold. We further design caged cytokines and receptor antagonists that are selectively activated by the designed proteases, enabling bioorthogonal control of cell state. Thus, de novo design can yield highly active, programmable proteases with applications in therapeutics, biotechnology and bioremediation.

title: Divergent genomic evolution in astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas
source: Nature
abstract: Astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas are isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-mutant gliomas that most commonly arise in adults under the age of 50 and exhibit variable responses to treatment1,2,3. To understand the genetic drivers of disease progression, here we used whole-genome and whole-exome sequencing to characterize longitudinally collected tumour specimens from 183 patients with IDH-mutant glioma. Samples were collected through the Glioma Longitudinal Analysis (GLASS) Consortium4. Most primary surgery samples were classified as grade 2 on the basis of histology (73% for astrocytomas and 93% for oligodendrogliomas). We validated known genomic markers of tumour progression, including hypermutation and homozygous deletion of CDKN2A or CDKN2B (hereafter, CDKN2A/B)5, and discovered genetic alterations that distinguish between the evolutionary trajectories of astrocytomas and those of oligodendrogliomas. Mutations in phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) and NOTCH1 were newly acquired in recurrent oligodendrogliomas, regardless of treatment, and were associated with an increased tumour mutational burden. In recurrent astrocytomas, however, again irrespective of treatment, acquired focal oncogene amplifications and CDKN2A/B homozygous deletions were associated with an increase in chromosomal imbalances, which converged with markers of chromosomal instability such as chromothripsis and whole-genome doubling. In both types of IDH-mutant glioma, we observed a convergence of acquired alterations, genome-wide changes and worse patient outcomes, suggesting that treatment-refractory clones were being selected. Treatment with temozolomide was associated with the mutational signatures SBS11 and SBS119 in both tumour types, whereas the radiotherapy-associated ID8 signature increased in astrocytomas specifically. We show that the genomes of oligodendrogliomas and astrocytomas adapt to the selective pressures of tumour progression and treatment in distinct ways, suggesting that oligodendrogliomas and astrocytomas differ in their responses to treatment-induced DNA damage.

title: Electric rectification by a redox-conductive metal-organic framework bilayer electrode
source: Chem
abstract: Redox-conductive metal-organic frameworks (RC-MOFs) combine molecularly tunable redox chemistry with crystalline, porous architectures. Stacking two RC-MOFs with different redox potentials creates a bilayer in which the direction of electron flow is governed by thermodynamically allowed interfacial redox reactions. This chemical rectification establishes RC-MOF bilayers as electrochemical diodes and provides a molecular strategy for programming directional charge transport.

title: Evaluating space-based methane detection through a one-year blind test
source: Nature
abstract: Space-based remote sensing allows detection and monitoring of large, concentrated methane sources worldwide1. However, independent evaluation of instruments and algorithms is limited, and new satellites and artificial intelligence techniques have not been tested under controlled, single-blind conditions2. Here we conduct a year-long, single-blind test involving 746 events: 481 methane releases of 9.5–1,183.7 kg h−1 and 265 blank controls. We released metered methane quantities in Arizona, USA, coinciding with overpasses from 12 government, commercial and non-profit satellites. Fifteen analysis teams from nine countries generated more than 2,250 estimates, making this, to our knowledge, the largest controlled test so far and one of the first evaluations of the instruments EMIT, Tanager-1 (Carbon Mapper) and GHOSt. Performance is heterogeneous: ‘built-for-purpose’ instruments designed to target methane demonstrate excellent detection performance (92–100% true positive rate, 0–11% false positive rate) and quantification accuracy (slope 0.83–1.00, 44% mean absolute percentage error). Instruments repurposed for methane sensing perform more variably (detection rates 62–88%, 46% mean absolute percentage error); still, many demonstrate significant skill. Broad land scanners detect poorly at tested rates but have consistent global coverage and historical archives, motivating additional work. Artificial intelligence-based methods show promise, but caution is warranted; 79% of false positives emerge from these methods. Ground-measured cloud cover >20% degraded performance across systems, raising concerns for use in some locations. Our findings show that satellite-based measurements can achieve accurate detection and quantification of methane point sources when the source location is approximately known.

title: Assessing green-growth and degrowth pathways through institutional regime feasibility
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Whether climate change policy should pursue green growth, degrowth, post-growth or agrowth cannot be settled by gross domestic product trajectories. The decisive issue is where each pathway places its heaviest burdens: on technology, well-being generation, energy demand, institutional capacity or political credibility. We extend the Kaya identity by decomposing energy intensity into the well-being generated per unit of output and the energy required per unit of well-being. The split locates stylized burden positions; a subsequent regime-feasibility test asks which institutions can generate and sustain the required movements, who bears costs and risks, and whether commitments remain credible over time.

title: Deciphering Critical Transition for AKI Deterioration by STIfuse: Fusing Dynamic and Static Representations
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a life-threatening condition with notably high in-hospital mortality, characterized by a three-phase progression: a relatively stable state (without imminent life threat), a critical pre-deterioration state (the time window which may be identified and in which timely intervention could prevent upcoming irreversible deterioration), and a deteriorated state (severe conditions such as death or rescue events). Accurate early prediction of AKI deterioration and deciphering the critical transition remain challenging because of complex, high-dimensional, noisy, and incomplete clinical data, as well as limited mechanistic understanding of disease progression. To solve this problem, we propose STIfuse (Spatiotemporal Information fusion), a unique dual-view framework that integrates deep learning (DL) and spatiotemporal information transformation (STI) based on Takens’ embedding theorem and critical slowing down (CSD) theory. The DL backbone encodes multi-dimensional static representations to capture structural dependencies, while the STI branch transforms high-dimensional spatial information into a low-dimensional dynamic representation. These views are fused by a multivariate Gaussian distribution: the means capture statistical levels for diagnosis, and the covariances reflect collective physiological fluctuations for early deterioration prediction. An optimal-transport-distance-based contrastive loss is employed to learn discriminative dynamic features between ˈcriticalˈ and ˈstableˈ states. Pretrained on the MIMIC-IV dataset and validated on five external cohorts (including MIMIC-III (with two independent cohorts), eICU, HiRID, and NWICU), STIfuse demonstrated superior performance in predicting 72-hour deterioration. Further analysis of single-cell multi-omics data study uncovered inflammatory cascades linking comorbidities to AKI. STIfuse provides an interpretable, robust and scalable framework for early warning of AKI deterioration prediction, highlighting its potential in utility and scalability for clinical foundation models.

title: Robust quasi-bound states in the continuum in bilayer terahertz metasurface with S4 point-group symmetry
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Metasurface-based bound states in the continuum (BICs) enable exceptional spatiotemporal control of light and substantially enhance light–matter interactions, making them highly attractive for applications in sensing, nonlinear optics, and integrated photonics. However, conventional BICs in single-layer metasurfaces rely on in-plane symmetry and are highly susceptible to structural perturbations, offering limited design flexibility and constraining both their robustness and functional diversity. To overcome these limitations, we theoretically propose and experimentally demonstrate a new class of symmetry-protected quasi-BICs in bilayer terahertz metasurfaces. These states are realized by coupling in-plane rotational and out-of-plane reflective symmetries through S4 point-group operations. Moreover, we show that such QBICs exhibit strong robustness against structural defects and fabrication imperfections. This work overcomes the robustness limitations of conventional single-layer metasurface BICs and establishes a general design paradigm for photonic devices that harness BICs with enhanced stability and scalability.

title: Unified structural origin of functionality in spiral skyrmions revealed by 3D electron tomography
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Ferroelectric skyrmions exhibit a range of emergent phenomena, including collective dynamics, negative capacitance, and a strong electric-field-induced second-harmonic generation response. However, three-dimensional (3D) atomic-scale configurations of skyrmions are unclarified yet, making the relationship between the physical functionalities and their underlying structural origin remains elusive. Here, using atomic-scale electron tomography, we experimentally resolve the 3D structure of polar skyrmion for the first time in PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattice. On the basis of large-data image acquisition with more than 95,000 3D coordinates of atoms, we visualize that the core of the skyrmions exhibit an upward spiraling morphology. By quantitatively analyzing the ferroelectric polarization and lattice distortion, we uncover an unconventional decoupling between the two at the skyrmion wall, where the polarization is suppressed, accompanied by a local enhancement of tetragonality exceeding 5% at the center of the wall. This increased tetragonality modifies the local free-energy landscape, enhancing the negative-capacitance response and field sensitivity at the skyrmion wall. The polar skyrmion wall hosts a concentration of emergent physical properties, thereby providing a unified structural origin for the functionalities and physical behaviors of skyrmions. This work establishes a real space basis for understanding the physical properties of polar skyrmions.

title: Photonic half-semimetals with dual semimetal-insulator topology
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Topological wave systems have largely evolved along two distinct paradigms: gapless topological semimetals and gapped topological insulators. While topological semimetals support bulk transport, they generally lack intrinsic selectivity among propagation channels; topological insulators enable robust transport but confine it to narrow interfaces, limiting spatial utilization. Here, we theoretically demonstrate and experimentally realize time-reversal-invariant spin-valley photonic half-semimetals (HSMs), which exhibit a dual semimetal-insulator topology within a single bulk band structure. In HSMs, the bandgap closes selectively in spin-valley space: for a given spin (valley), one valley (spin) is semimetallic while the other remains insulating. This coexistence of spin- and valley-resolved gapless and gapped band structures makes HSMs fundamentally distinct from both conventional semimetals and insulators. As a defining bulk phenomenon, an HSM functions as a spin-valley-locked beam splitter, intrinsically enabling valley-selective spin routing. Moreover, when four complementary HSMs are assembled into a periodic superlattice, the same dual topology enables reciprocal spin-valley-resolved multilane helical transport with 100% spatial utilization. These results establish HSMs as a platform for selective bulk wave control and multichannel topological transport beyond conventional topological phases.

title: Jurassic flightless bird reveals early ecological diversity of avialans
source: Nature
abstract: The origin and early diversification of birds remain highly debated in vertebrate evolution. Although estimates of the evolutionary timescales suggest a Jurassic period radiation1,2, a profound scarcity of fossils from this period has hampered how the distinctive bird bauplan was assembled3,4,5. Selection for powered flight has been viewed as the primary driver of early avialan skeletal modifications3,6,7, attesting to the independent occurrences of aerodynamic features among paravian lineages8. Here we report on the discovery of a Late Jurassic avialan, Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis, gen. et sp. nov., from the Zhenghe Fauna of southeastern China9. As one of the earliest diverging avialans, Y. yangyuanensis exhibits a striking mosaic of features, combining a mixture of avialan- and troodontid-like cranial characters, paired with derived postcranial traits and a deinonychosaur-like hyperextensible second pedal digit. Phylogenetically informed analyses show that Y. yangyuanensis possesses markedly short forelimbs—a condition present widely among non-avialan theropods. These findings provide strong evidence for a terrestrial, flightless lifestyle of Y. yangyuanensis. Our study demonstrates that evolution works intensively as exemplified by the occurrence of several, divergent ecological pathways being exploited in the initial diversification of birds.

title: Advancing subseasonal forecasting with machine learning
source: Nature
abstract: Decision-makers rely on weather forecasts to plant crops, manage wildfires, allocate water and energy and prepare for weather extremes1,2,3. Today, such forecasts enjoy unprecedented accuracy as far as 2 weeks thanks to steady advances in physics-based dynamical models and data-driven artificial intelligence models4,5,6,7,8,9,10. However, model skill drops precipitously at subseasonal timescales (2–6 weeks ahead) due to compounding errors, systemic model biases and the chaotic nature of the atmosphere11,12,13,14,15. To counter this degradation, we introduce probabilistic bias correction, a machine learning framework that substantially reduces systematic error by learning to correct historical probabilistic forecasts. When applied to the leading dynamical and artificial intelligence models from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), probabilistic bias correction doubles the modest subseasonal skill of the AI Forecasting System16 and improves the skill of the operationally debiased dynamical model17 for 91% of pressure, 92% of temperature and 98% of precipitation targets. We designed probabilistic bias correction for operational deployment, and, in the 2025 real-time forecasting competition of ECMWF18, its global forecasts were the best for all weather variables and lead times, outperforming the dynamical models from six operational forecasting centres, an international dynamical multimodel ensemble, the AI Forecasting System of ECMWF and the forecasting systems of 34 teams worldwide. These probabilistic skill gains translate into more accurate prediction of extreme events and have the potential to improve agricultural planning, energy management and disaster preparedness in vulnerable communities19.

title: Evidence of large-scale and room-temperature stair-stepped quantum spin Hall states in Bi4Br4
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Topological insulators host exotic quantum phenomena such as the quantum spin Hall (QSH) effect, which enables dissipationless one-dimensional edge conduction. Realizing such states at room temperature and on a macroscopic scale is essential for energy-efficient electronics and quantum technologies, yet remains a fundamental challenge due to material limitations. Here, using microwave impedance microscopy, we directly visualize robust conductive channels persisting up to 300 K in α-Bi4Br4 nanowires. Their stability and scalability are likely enabled by a “stair-stepped” stacking configuration on the side facets, a multilayer geometry in which QSH edge states from individual layers remain spatially decoupled. This configuration circumvents the stringent alignment and layer-number constraints of previous proposals, allowing robust stair-stepped QSH (SS-QSH) conduction in structures several micrometers long and hundreds of nanometers high. Magnetic-field- and temperature-dependent measurements are consistent with the topological nature of these conductive channels, as further supported by our theoretical analysis. Crucially, the conductance peaks and bulk signals scale with nanowire height, verifying the stair-stepped origin. Our results are also successfully reproduced by finite-element analysis simulations. This work establishes α-Bi4Br4 as a practical platform for high-temperature topological electronics and demonstrates a generalizable stacking strategy for designing scalable QSH systems.

title: Metal-organic pulsed laser deposition for complex oxide heterostructures
source: Matter
abstract: Point defects govern the properties of complex oxides, yet they are hard to control precisely. Lee et al. introduce metal-organic pulsed laser deposition (MOPLD), which tunes the cation stoichiometry of SrTiO3 films to within a 0.1% solubility limit. By selectively adjusting antisite and vacancy populations, MOPLD suppresses oxygen vacancies and boosts the low-temperature mobility of the LaAlO3/SrTiO3 electron gas, offering a general route to defect engineering in oxide heterostructures for quantum materials research.

title: Educational intervention can rewire village social networks
source: Nature
abstract: Social networks shape behaviour, affect information dissemination and undergird collective action. And they can be exploited in the design of interventions in these domains1,2,3,4,5,6,7. Although social networks obey fundamental principles, such as the degree distribution8,9, they can nevertheless evolve as ties form and break. Here, through a randomized controlled trial involving a total of 8,331 people in 110 remote Honduran villages, we evaluate the secondary effects of a 22-month public-health intervention1 on pre-existing social-network structure. We used a design in which a varying fraction of village households received the intervention, and villages in which no one received the intervention were used as the primary reference group. In ‘low-dosage’ villages (in which 5–30% of households received the intervention), people who received the intervention tended to sever ties with untreated individuals to whom they previously went for health advice. Conversely, in high-dosage villages (50–100%), treated individuals increased their ties. These average changes are explained mainly by tie dynamics; that is, treated–treated pairs persist and form new links, whereas treated–untreated ties dissolve. A mediation analysis indicates that absorption of health information increases the likelihood of tie formation and persistence. The rewiring patterns generally lasted for three years after the intervention ceased. Moreover, although the intervention delivered health information, it reshaped friendship and financial ties, not just health-advice connections. In aggregate, the introduction of a new information regime acted as a kind of social institution, rewiring individuals’ connections even though the overall degree distribution of village-wide networks remained relatively stable.

title: Structural basis of ligand recognition and gating in mosquito IRs
source: Nature
abstract: Ionotropic receptors (IRs) are essential for insect olfaction, enabling the detection of carboxylic acids, amines, moisture, and temperature cues that mediate critical behaviors, including mosquito host-seeking 1,2. However, the structural mechanisms underlying ligand specificity and channel activation in these receptors remain unclear. Here, we report cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures and functional validation of the IR8a-IR75k complex from the malaria mosquito Anopheles stephensi, a carboxylic acid detector, captured in four states: the ligand-free full-length closed form (apo state), the ligand induced full-length open state, and the nonanoic acid (NA)- and octanoic acid (OA)-bound extracellular domains. These structures reveal a dynamic ligand-binding pocket in IR75k, in which specificity is determined by alkyl chain length and carboxylate geometry. Ligand binding triggers closure of IR75k’s bilobed ligand binding domain (LBD), and this conformational change propagates through conserved mechanical linkers to the transmembrane domain (TMD), functioning as a molecular lever that dilates the pore via outward displacement of transmembrane helices. This gating mechanism was further corroborated by molecular dynamics simulations and electrophysiology. These insights provide an atomic resolution view of IR mediated host detection in mosquitoes and establish a foundation for the rational design of next generation mosquito control strategies targeting host-seeking behavior.

title: Overlooked brown fat in our bodies linked to wide range of health benefits
source: Nature

title: Can weakly interlayer-coupled transition metal dichalcogenides open up a new prospect of two-dimensional family?
source: Matter
abstract: Weak interlayer coupling, originating from electron interactions of adjacent layers, can provide promising prospects for two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), which can be respectively evaluated by energy criteria qualitatively and by band-gap transformation and band-shifting ratios quantitatively. Weakly interlayer-coupled TMDCs will promote the development of all-2D processing-in-memory devices together with strongly interlayer-coupled ones.

title: Sexual dimorphism in epidermal stem cell dynamics
source: Nature
abstract: The epidermis is a stratified epithelium comprising proliferative basal cells and differentiated suprabasal cells that are continuously renewed throughout life. Conflicting theories have been proposed regarding the heterogeneity of the basal cell layer, with some studies proposing that all proliferative cells have self-renewal potential during homeostasis1,2,3,4,5. Meanwhile, others posit a model in which stem cell differentiation occurs through an intermediate transit-amplifying-like progenitor state with strictly limited proliferative potential6,7,8,9,10. Here, to determine the heterogeneity and pattern of cell fate, we performed intravital time-lapse imaging to track the fate of lineage-labelled cells in the skin interfollicular epidermis. Results from quantitative analyses of clonal dynamics support a two-compartment model of epidermal homeostasis, whereby basal cells are organized in a stem cell–transit-amplifying cell hierarchy. Critical to these conclusions was the discovery of sexual dimorphism in epidermal fate, with female mice showing a highly synchronized pattern of cell division, differentiation and delamination that contributes to accelerated wound healing. Single-cell RNA sequencing, transcriptional profiling and clonal analyses of castrated mice revealed that male sex hormones promote stem cell differentiation and delamination. In summary, our study provides insight into the functional identity of the stem cell population and identifies sex-specific differences in the regulation of epidermal stem cells and transit-amplifying cell fate.

title: Sliding ferroelectricity scales up
source: Nature Nanotechnology

title: A microexon regulatory code reveals autism-linked genetic variation
source: Nature
abstract: Neuronal microexons are a highly conserved class of alternative splicing events enriched in genes with critical functions in nervous system biology1,2. Microexon splicing is often disrupted in the brains of autistic individuals, and mice with microexon deficiencies display autism-like phenotypes1,3,4. However, the full landscape of microexons is not known, and the impact of genetic variation on these exons has not been systematically investigated. Here, through extensive transcriptome profiling, we detect hundreds of new microexons, including many with neuronal subtype-specific splicing patterns, and others that activate nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. Using machine learning, we define a sequence code predictive of neuronally spliced microexons and use this to identify critical regulatory elements surrounding the expanded microexon repertoire. This code further reveals genomic variants predicted to alter microexon splicing in individuals affected by autism, with rare variants having the strongest estimated impact. These variants are mostly detected in idiopathic individuals and are associated with autism status. They also converge on synaptic and other autism-linked genes, as well as genes not previously linked to autism. Our results collectively define an expanded repertoire of microexons, delineate their regulatory code, and pinpoint variants predicted to affect their splicing, with implications for the disruption of functions central to neuronal biology and brain disorders.

title: Thermodynamic decoupling of polymer pre-aggregation in sustainable solvents enables high-detectivity flexible organic photodiodes
source: Matter
abstract: Precise control of solution aggregation enables flexible organic photodiodes processed from sustainable solvents to combine high detectivity with strong mechanical durability. By slowing rapid nucleation and improving film formation, this approach reduces trap formation and structural defects, offering a practical route toward sustainably manufactured wearable optoelectronics.

title: Electrochemical energy conversion beyond Earth
source: Joule
abstract: Terrestrial electrochemical design implicitly relies on Earth-bound physics, such as gravity and natural convection. Beyond Earth, where these conditions no longer apply, we argue that designing with architecture, co-integrating electrochemical, thermal, and mechanical functions into a single structure, emerges as a primary physical variable rather than a downstream choice. Furthermore, additive manufacturing enables rapid structural iteration, allowing electrochemical energy conversion devices to be tailored to the strict operational demands of both space environments and resource-limited terrestrial applications.

title: How early tetrapods got their neck
source: Nature

title: Generation and Stabilization of Soliton‐Type Radicals in Amidine‐Linked Porous Oligoacetylene Polymers by Topological Confinement Strategy for Photothermal Catalysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Porous polymers incorporating stable organic radicals are typically limited to a handful of known radical types. Here, we introduce a topological confinement strategy that generates a previously inaccessible class of open‑shell species: neutral soliton‑type radicals, within amidine‑linked oligoacetylene networks. In chemical terms, these species are characterized by a delocalized spin density over the conjugated backbone, distinguishing them from conventional localized radicals. These materials exhibit a distinct axial
                    g
                    ‑tensor, Curie behavior, and broad near‑infrared absorption extending to 1000 nm. Unlike conventional photothermal systems, where heat originates from exciton transfer energy to the lattice via nonradiative processes, our system stores light energy in long‐lived soliton states that dissipate via lattice vibrations, producing no ground‑state bleach yet enabling efficient heat generation. Using this mechanism, the materials drive aldehyde‑indole coupling under mild light irradiation through a photothermal catalytic pathway. More broadly, this work translates soliton physics into a synthetic materials platform for spin‑functional materials.

title: Architecting 3D Space‐Charge Heterointerfacial Networks for Electrode‐Scale Ion Transport
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Harnessing space‐charge effects to govern carrier dynamics is central to nanoionics, yet translating localized nanoscale transport into continuous electrode‐wide percolation remains challenging. Here, we report an architectural strategy that uses Na
                    2
                    O/Na
                    2
                    CO
                    3
                    heterointerfaces as local nanoionic transport units and organizes them into a bulk‐distributed, three‐dimensional network throughout a preformed electrode. This architecture is realized by coupling ultralow‐flux Na‐vapor metallization with mesopore‐regulated gas‐solid conversion in a preformed metal‐organic framework (MOF) host. The synergy of space‐charge carrier enrichment and MOF‐mediated lattice distortion simultaneously boosts carrier density and lowers migration barriers, yielding an estimated local interfacial conductivity on the order of 10
                    −7
                    S cm
                    −1
                    at 25°C, from intrinsically insulating Na
                    2
                    O (10
                    −12
                    S cm
                    −1
                    ) and Na
                    2
                    CO
                    3
                    (10
                    −23
                    S cm
                    −1
                    ). Integrated with conducting carbon, this functionally percolating network enables stable solid‐state presodiation and ultrahigh‐rate sodium‐ion full cells. This work bridges the gap between nanoscopic interface physics and macroscopic device functionality, identifying the spatial connectivity of phase boundaries, rather than the localized space‐charge effect alone, as a programmable design variable for next‐generation solid‐state ionics.

title: Hierarchically Molecular Programming of Antiparallel H‑Aggregates for NIR Type I Photochemistry
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Developing near‐infrared (NIR) photosensitizers with effective type I reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation remains challenging. H‑aggregates promote triplet formation and charge transfer, but often suffer from substantial absorption blueshifts and excessive thermal deactivation that compromise photosensitization efficacy. Herein, a hierarchically molecular programming strategy is proposed to construct minimal‐blueshift H‐aggregates as robust NIR type I photosensitizers. Primary engineering via π‐bridge extension and acceptor strengthening within a twisted–planar donor–π–acceptor scaffold endows the antiparallel H‐packed TNCF3‐C6‐C2 aggregates with strong NIR absorption (749 nm) and predominant type I ROS generation. Secondary side‐chain programming further regulates the H‐packing and intermolecular electronic interactions to enhance type I ROS generation. Structural, photochemical and theoretical investigations revealed that the branched side chains promote molecular planarization and robust H‑packing, thereby enhancing intersystem crossing and intermolecular charge transfer. The optimized TNCF3‐2C6 with symmetric branched side chain exhibited minimal absorption blueshift (20 nm) upon H‐aggregation, enhanced NIR harvesting ability and a further ∼2‐fold enhancement in ROS generation over the initial TNCF3‐C6‐C2 H‐aggregates, thereby delivering potent tumor inhibition both in vitro and in vivo. Built upon the hierarchical programming of H‐aggregates, this work establishes a supramolecular design paradigm toward modulating excitonic coupling and excited‐state dynamics for high‐performance photo‐functional materials.

title: Perturbation of the Electron Transport Chain by Guanidinium‐Based Cationic Polymers Induces Metabolic Collapse in Persister‐Enriched Bacterial Populations
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Bacterial persisters are widely regarded as dormant or hypometabolic cells that survive antibiotic treatment with suppressed metabolic activity. Here, we show that this apparent quiescence is accompanied by a heightened vulnerability to electron transport chain (ETC)‐associated perturbation by guanidinium‐based cationic polymers. PO
                    3
                    G, a representative polymer, preferentially kills persister‐enriched populations while markedly perturbing respiratory electron transfer. Following this ETC‐associated perturbation, persister‐enriched populations exhibit sustained superoxide‐associated oxidative stress and fail to restore NADH/NAD
                    +
                    homeostasis, leading to progressive loss of viability. Consistent with this ETC dependency, PO
                    3
                    G also markedly reduces persister‐enriched population induced by diverse triggers across bacterial species and achieves up to 7‐log reductions in bacterial burden in vivo. These results establish a mechanistic link between cationic polymer‐induced ETC‐associated perturbation and persister elimination, highlighting limited recovery from respiratory and redox perturbation as a vulnerability underlying the preferential killing of persisters.

title: Integrative multi-omics reveals CUL4B as a modulator of macrophage pyroptosis and innate defense against Staphylococcus aureus
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Staphylococcus aureus
                    (SA) causes a broad range of invasive human diseases, increasingly complicated by antibiotic resistance. Macrophages (MΦ) play a central role in innate immunity, yet key aspects of their interaction with SA remain incompletely understood because of the pathogen’s diverse immune evasion strategies. Using multi-omics and systems-level analytics, we identified the E3 ubiquitin ligase cullin 4B (CUL4B) as a host factor that modulates MΦ responses to SA infection. CRISPR-mediated deletion of CUL4B in human THP-1 MΦ enhanced intracellular bacterial killing, reduced cell death, decreased caspase-1 activation, and lowered interleukin-1β production, consistent with altered inflammasome signaling. In a murine methicillin-resistant SA (MRSA) pneumonia model, CUL4B deficiency improved pulmonary bacterial clearance, reduced bacteremia, and decreased inflammatory tissue injury. Whole-lung and serum proteomics further revealed increased antimicrobial protein abundance and reduced markers of inflammatory damage. Together, these findings identify CUL4B as a regulator of MΦ inflammatory responses during MRSA infection and suggest a potential host-directed pathway that could be leveraged to improve outcomes against this major pathogen.

title: Bioinspired supramolecular thermistor for resolving subtle temperature variations
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Precise detection of subtle temperature variations under cryogenic conditions is critical for environmental monitoring but remains challenging because conventional thermistors suffer from limited sensitivity and mechanical interference. Here, we report a bioinspired supramolecular thermistor that achieves thermal transduction through molecularly gated charge transport. The hybrid polyurethane/carboxymethyl cellulose (PU/CMC)/MXene/NiO composite integrates dynamic hydrogen-bond reconfiguration, hydrated ionic conduction, and temperature-dependent electronic transport. Upon cooling, cooperative supramolecular evolution continuously modulates coupled ionic and electronic pathways, producing an ultrahigh negative temperature coefficient of −22,280% °C
                    −1
                    between −80° and −75°C. The thermistor resolves detectable temperature changes below 0.01°C while maintaining negligible hysteresis, excellent reproducibility, and effective thermal-mechanical decoupling. Combined with a dedicated low-noise readout circuit, it enables reliable monitoring of subtle temperature evolution during simulated atmospheric cooling. Integrated into a multichannel sensor array, it further provides force-independent thermal mapping for robotic manipulation. This work establishes molecularly gated supramolecular thermal transduction as a strategy for ultrahigh-resolution cryogenic temperature sensing.

title: From scrap to prime: Designing high-performance alloys from dirty feedstocks with machine learning
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Producing alloys from recycled metals via secondary synthesis can markedly cut energy use, greenhouse-gas emissions, and dependence on scarce, strategically important elements relative to primary routes. The central obstacle is the feedstock itself: Scrap is chemically heterogeneous and unpredictable, a “dirty” mix whose impurities typically embrittle materials. Conventional strategies address this challenge by diluting impurities through the addition of virgin material, thereby restricting scrap utilization, limiting microstructural design freedom, and undermining cost and sustainability benefits. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different, data-driven paradigm that deliberately reverses a five-millennia-old metallurgical injunction: Rather than purifying the alloy, we design the alloy to accommodate and exploit its contaminants. Using a model ductile iron representative of 120 million metric tons of heavily contaminated scrap, we couple experiments with deep-neural-network optimization to identify chemically robust, impurity-tolerant processing windows. The resulting “dirty” irons retain ductility and strength by integrating impurity effects into a purposeful microstructure, rather removing them. The approach achieves complete recyclability, an 8.1% reduction in manufacturing cost, and mechanical gains of up to 15.2% in ultimate tensile strength and 73.2% in elongation at fracture. Crucially, it overcomes the canonical strength-ductility trade-off while enabling far greater scrap utilization and material circularity. By endowing alloys with a practical “gene of scrap compatibility,” this strategy reframes alloy design for a resource-constrained future and advances a mass-conserving circular economy for metals.

title: Nanoconfinement-cooperated catalysis enables rapid tandem redox kinetics for wide-temperature lithium-sulfur batteries
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The slow kinetics of sulfur cathodes caused by the high energy barriers of Li
                    +
                    desolvation stem primarily from the structure of the inner Helmholtz plane (IHP). Herein, a synergistic strategy combining electrochemical tandem catalysis with spatial nanoconfinement is proposed to regulate the Li(solvent)
                    
                      x
                    
                    +
                    dynamics. As a proof-of-concept, the porous covalent organic framework (denoted as TPBD) decorated MXene is in situ constructed, acting as a tandem kinetic promoter. The theoretical simulations and in situ Raman reveal that the porous TPBD layer confines the bulky Li(solvent)
                    
                      x
                    
                    +
                    species and sieves the spatial structure with accelerated Li
                    +
                    diffusion kinetics. Meanwhile, MXene serves as a negatively charged substrate that helps disrupt anion-solvent interactions and reconstruct the solvation structure at the IHP, thereby enhancing Li
                    +
                    kinetics and sulfur redox reversibility. Encouragingly, the assembled cells demonstrate a superior Li
                    +
                    transference number (0.77), long-term cycling lifespan up to 1000 cycles, as well as excellent areal capacity (>6 mAh cm
                    −2
                    ) at 0°C and superior rate capability at 50°C under a high sulfur loading of 7.51 mg cm
                    −2
                    . The as-prepared pouch cell remains stable for over 100 cycles, validating this novel integration of catalysis and nanoconfinement for tandem kinetics in Li-S batteries.

title: Emergent coherent-incoherent phonon crossover enables ultralow lattice thermal conductivity in 3D double perovskite
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The interplay between coherent (wave-like) and incoherent (particle-like) phonon transport is central to heat conduction, yet experimental evidence of their crossover in bulk three-dimensional (3D) crystals remains scarce. Here, we report intrinsically ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (
                    
                      
                        
                          
                            κ
                            l
                          
                        
                      
                    
                    ) in the lead-free double perovskite Cs
                    2
                    AgBiCl
                    6
                    , reaching 0.52 and 0.28 W m
                    −1
                     K
                    −1
                    in single crystal and polycrystals, respectively, at room temperature. Combining thermal transport, low-temperature heat capacity, Raman spectroscopy, synchrotron x-ray pair distribution function analysis, and anharmonic lattice-dynamics calculations, we uncover the microscopic origin of this anomalous heat transport. Chemical bonding heterogeneity, weakly bound rattling-like Cs vibrations, anisotropic Cl dynamics, and soft lattice modes generate low-energy localized optical phonons that strongly interact with acoustic modes. Enhanced three- and four-phonon scattering suppresses phonon lifetimes, while anharmonic renormalization flattens optical branches and reduces group velocities. Coherent contributions account for ∼50% of
                    
                      
                        
                          
                            κ
                            l
                          
                        
                      
                    
                    near room temperature and exceeding incoherent contributions above ∼200 K, revealing an emergent coherent-incoherent phonon crossover in a fully crystalline 3D solid.

title: Mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase–VB inhibition rescues brain endothelial stress and memory in Alzheimer’s disease models
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative disorder with no effective cure, characterized by the cerebral parenchymal and vascular accumulation of aggregated amyloid-β (Aβ) and hyperphosphorylated tau. Cerebrovascular and mitochondria dysfunction are early causal events in the progression of AD. Previous studies support that inhibiting carbonic anhydrases (CAs) may prevent mitochondrial and cerebrovascular dysfunction in AD models. Here, we selectively target the mitochondrial CA isoform CA-VB by pharmacological and genetic manipulation in human cerebral microvascular endothelial cells (hCMEC), and we confirm the protective effects of the CA-V inhibitor in AD mice. CA-V inhibition and CA-VB KO prevent Aβ induced mitochondria-mediated endothelial apoptosis, loss of barrier resistance, and hCMEC inflammatory activation. Strikingly, CA-V inhibition also mitigates caspase activation and endothelial cell activation in the brains of 3xTg AD mice, resulting in preserved memory function. Our results demonstrate that selective CA-V inhibition is an effective and promising strategy against AD-mediated cerebrovascular pathology, neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment.

title: Bisulfate-mediated selective methane oxidation under mild aqueous conditions
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The selective oxidation of methane under mild conditions remains a formidable challenge because of the inert C─H bond and the ease of over-oxidation. Here we report a facile strategy that enables methane conversion at room temperature and ambient pressure using molecular O
                    2
                    and commercially available Cu powder in dilute aqueous H
                    2
                    SO
                    4
                    . The reaction is capable of proceeding with only trace CO
                    2
                    formation, producing methyl bisulfate and methanol as the primary partial oxidation products. In situ Raman spectroscopy indicates that an in situ O
                    2
                    -derived Cu
                    2
                    O surface is the reaction-relevant phase associated with C─H bond activation. The observed selectivity arises from bisulfate adsorption on this Cu
                    2
                    O surface, which suppresses methanol over-oxidation, together with the interception of surface-generated methyl intermediates to form oxidation-resistant methyl bisulfate. This Cu/O
                    2
                    -H
                    2
                    SO
                    4
                    system demonstrates that methane can be selectively oxidized under mild aqueous conditions and provides mechanistic insight into Cu/O
                    2
                    -mediated oxidation, suggesting a bisulfate-assisted approach to suppressing over-oxidation that may be applicable to other substrates.

title: A fast and frugal Gaussian boson sampling emulator
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Classical algorithms have successfully reproduced expectation values of observables for certain quantum circuits using off-the-shelf computing resources; however, matching the performance of the most advanced quantum devices on sampling problems typically incurs extreme memory and computational costs, restricting such simulations to only a handful of supercomputers worldwide. In this work, we demonstrate a classical simulation outperforming Gaussian boson sampling experiments of 100 modes on established benchmark tests using a single central processing unit (CPU) or graphics processing unit (GPU). Being embarrassingly parallelizable, a small number of CPUs or GPUs allows us to match previous sampling rates that required more than 100 GPUs. We believe that algorithmic and implementation improvements have the potential to generalize our tools to photocounting and pseudo–photon number–resolving scenarios and larger system sizes. Last, most of the innovations in our tools remain valid for generic probability distributions over binary variables, rendering them potentially applicable to the simulation of qubit-based sampling problems and creating classical surrogates for classical-quantum algorithms.

title: A B1 SINE element within the mouse Malat1 long noncoding RNA acts as an internal ribosome entry site mediating micropeptide translation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
In most cells,
                    Malat1
                    long noncoding RNA localizes to the nucleus where it affects splicing and chromatin function. In mouse neurons,
                    Malat1
                    is exported to the cytoplasm where it is translated to generate the M1 micropeptide. Here, we characterize an internal ribosome entry site (IRES) required for M1 translation that is sufficient to induce cap-independent expression of a downstream open reading frame. In vivo chemical probing and structural modeling defined a three-stem-loop RNA secondary structure that encompasses the active IRES segment and coincides with a mouse B1 SINE (short interspersed element) repetitive element. In affinity purification experiments, a minimal IRES/B1 RNA selectively bound ribosomal subunits, translation factors, and the known IRES cofactors Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1. Depletion of Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1 inhibited IRES-dependent translation of the reporter and expression of the endogenous M1 peptide. Our study identifies an unexpected functional unit hidden within a widely studied long noncoding RNA.

title: Global conservation additionality hindered by persisting fishing pressure in marine protected areas
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Marine protected areas (MPAs) are the cornerstone of global marine conservation strategies. Yet, their capacity to achieve conservation gains (i.e., conservation additionality) hinges on the decrease in human threats to biodiversity within their boundary, a feature rarely measured or reported. Here, we test a central but underexamined question in global conservation policy: Have MPA implementations actually reduced within-boundary fishing pressure, currently the main direct human threat to marine biodiversity? Using a stratified before-after-control-impact approach, we investigated 861 MPAs of varying levels of protection across all ocean basins, representing half of global MPA coverage, and found that most implementations were not followed by decreases in industrial fishing effort. Protection levels strongly predicted the direction and magnitude of relative changes in fishing effort after implementation. Only fully protected areas were associated with significant decreases in fishing effort within boundaries. Highly protected areas were only associated with lower rates of increase in fishing effort within compared to outside boundaries. Both fully and highly protected areas were implemented in areas experiencing initial low fishing effort, reducing the overall abatement in fishing effort achieved. Conversely, areas with higher initial fishing effort tended to be attributed to MPAs with low levels of protection, also limiting abatement. Larger MPAs were associated with greater decreases in fishing effort, while time since implementation had no significant effect. Complementing targets of protection coverage and protection levels with conservation additionality targets, such as pressure abatement, could shift incentives from quantity to effectiveness of interventions and ensure positive biodiversity conservation outcomes.

title: A transcriptional cofactor GRIP1 drives PPARγ DNA binding and p300-dependent enhancer activity during homeostatic macrophage polarization
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Homeostatic macrophages maintain tissue health and resolve inflammation. Upon sustained exposure to type II cytokine IL4, transcription factors STAT6, KLF4, EGR2 and a ligand-regulated nuclear receptor PPARγ orchestrate the M2
                    IL4
                    ‘polarization’, marked by enhancer RNA (eRNA) production near multiple M2 genes. The mechanisms of enhancer activation by unliganded PPARγ are poorly understood. We interrogated cofactor requirements for PPARγ-driven gene expression in M2
                    IL4
                    , including those lacking PPARγ or a ligand-dependent nuclear receptor coregulator NCoA2/GRIP1 vs. macrophages treated with the PPARγ agonist rosiglitazone. As expected, rosiglitazone activated conventional PPARγ targets; GRIP1 deletion blunted their induction and depleted GRIP1-interacting histone acetyltransferase p300 from PPARγ-bound sites. Surprisingly, GRIP1 colocalized with unliganded PPARγ in M0 and M2
                    IL4
                    , and GRIP1 ablation dramatically reduced genome-wide DNA binding of PPARγ itself while promoting broad deposition of CTCF insulator. Functionally, GRIP1 deletion mirrored PPARγ deficiency, establishing GRIP1 as a central regulator of unliganded PPARγ DNA binding, required for both eRNA and mRNA transcription of PPARγ targets in homeostatic macrophages.

title: TIME FOR COFFEE coordinates phase separation and chromatin regulation for salt tolerance
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The circadian clock enhances plant fitness by aligning internal timing with the external photoperiod, but how it coordinates spatiotemporal regulation with chromatin dynamics to improve salt tolerance is not well understood. Here, we show that the clock component TIME FOR COFFEE (TIC) forms biomolecular condensates in response to salt stress, but not to osmotic stress alone. Consistently,
                    tic
                    mutants were hypersensitive to salt stress yet displayed enhanced salt tolerance under 21-hour light-dark cycles matching their shortened circadian period, highlighting the importance of circadian clock in salt tolerance. Salt stress increases H3K9ac levels at the salt stress–responsive genes and induces their expression in a time-of-day–dependent manner in wild-type plants, whereas both H3K9ac level and transcriptional activation are attenuated in
                    tic
                    mutants. TIC physically associates with HD2-type histone deacetylases, and a subset of HD2 partially colocalizes with TIC condensates in the nucleolus under salt stress. Genetic and biochemical analyses showed that salt stress promotes TIC condensate formation, accompanied by reduced HD2 occupancy at salt stress–responsive loci, thereby elevating H3K9ac levels and promoting gene expression. Together, these findings uncover a mechanism by which salt-induced TIC condensate formation links chromatin regulation with circadian timing, thereby promoting plant adaptation to salt stress.

title: Vitamin D binding protein in ventral CA3 of the hippocampus drives stress-induced depression
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The ventral hippocampus plays a crucial role in regulating emotional and motivated behaviors. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its dysfunction in major depressive disorder (MDD) remain poorly understood. Here, we identified elevated expression of vitamin D binding protein (VDBP) in the hippocampi of chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)–susceptible mice, which correlated with the severity of depression-like behaviors. Notably, VDBP up-regulation was specifically in ventral CA3 excitatory (vCA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    ) neurons. CA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    VDBP overexpression led to inhibited neuronal activity, synaptic and dendritic impairments, and, ultimately, depression-like behaviors. Conversely, vCA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    -specific VDBP knockdown enhanced resilience to chronic stress. Mechanistically, VDBP directly interacted with PIK3R3 to inhibit the PI3K-Akt-mTOR pathway in a cell-autonomous manner, leading to excessive autophagy and subsequent neuronal dysfunction. Chemogenetic activation, intervention using the Akt-specific activator SC79, and site-specific mutation disrupting the VDBP-PIK3R3 interaction ameliorated vCA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    VDBP-induced depression-like phenotypes. Collectively, these findings underscore the critical involvement of vCA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    neuron–derived VDBP in stress-induced depressive pathology and highlight its potential as a therapeutic target for MDD.

title: Maternal vaccination with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugates protects against murine Klebsiella pneumoniae neonatal sepsis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Klebsiella pneumoniae
                    is the leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and the foremost cause of infectious deaths in young children.
                    K. pneumoniae
                    isolates are becoming increasingly resistant to antibiotics, creating a great need for additional therapies or preventative strategies. Maternal vaccination serves as an attractive approach to protect from
                    K. pneumoniae
                    neonatal sepsis. Herein, we report a murine model of maternal immunization followed by pup challenge to evaluate putative
                    K. pneumoniae
                    vaccines. Dams were immunized with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugate vaccines at mating and boosted with two different immunization schedules throughout the gestational period. After parturition, offspring were tested for antigen-specific antibody levels and later challenged with a lethal dose of
                    K. pneumoniae.
                    Pups born to dams immunized with K1- and K2-conjugate vaccines demonstrated significant protection from sepsis relative to control pups. Antibodies transferred from vaccinated dams persisted and remained protective in pups for at least six weeks after birth. Collectively these results demonstrate a feasible and reproducible murine model of maternal immunization verifying the efficacy of bioconjugate vaccines in protecting against lethal neonatal
                    K. pneumoniae
                    infection.

title: Bedrock erodibility governs transient erosion and CO2 release in alpine landscapes
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Differences in lithology within alpine watersheds lead to strong contrasts in bedrock erodibility, which modulate climatic and tectonic influences on erosion, chemical weathering, and carbon dioxide exchange. However, the difficulty of measuring denudation rates in fine-grained rocks has limited our ability to quantify the magnitude of erodibility differences between weak sedimentary and strong igneous rocks. Here, we combine newly developed cosmogenic beryllium-10 measurements in shale with conventional beryllium-10 measurements in intrusive rocks, topographic analysis, solute data, and landscape evolution modeling in the East River watershed, Colorado. Shale-dominated catchments denude three times faster than adjacent intrusive catchments despite having gentler topography. Hydrochemical data and modeling indicate that elevated shale denudation enhances solute generation and net inorganic weathering–driven carbon dioxide release during prolonged landscape adjustment over million-year timescales. These results show that spatial variability in rock type alone can substantially alter the carbon dioxide balance of alpine landscapes by hiding the fastest erosion rates in relatively gentle terrain.

title: Reversible Atlantic overturning despite continued Greenland ice sheet melt
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is considered vulnerable to irreversible weakening or collapse under global warming and related Greenland ice sheet (GrIS) melt, yet its resilience to either forcing remains poorly constrained. Here, we use a carbon dioxide emission–driven Earth system model with an interactive GrIS to assess AMOC reversibility under a range of idealized carbon dioxide emission pathways that produce near-linear global warming up to 10 kelvins (K), stabilization across 1.5 to 9 K, and subsequent cooling. We find that although the AMOC reaches threshold-defined collapsed states, these do not represent dynamical tipping in this model: The overturning weakens quasi-linearly with global mean temperature increase yet consistently and promptly recovers under cooling. In contrast, GrIS mass loss accelerates with warming, continues through stabilizations, and is only slowed by cooling, committing the planet to long-term sea level rise. These results reveal contrasting resilience across climate system components: Under transient carbon dioxide forcing, AMOC strength remains dynamically reversible despite continued Greenland meltwater input, whereas the GrIS is locked into persistent decline. Our findings underscore the urgency of rapid emission cuts to limit climate overshoot, AMOC weakening, and irreversible ice sheet loss.

title: Comprehensive characterization of transposable element expression reveals regulatory circuitry and clinical implications in cancers
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) constitute nearly half of the human genome and have crucial roles in regulatory networks and clinical utility in cancers. However, the expression profiles at a single-element resolution remain unexplored. By integrating multiomics data from ∼10,000 samples and 1000 cancer cell lines, we established an expression atlas of 95,512 individual TEs across 980 subfamilies. Transcription factors and RNA binding proteins that are broadly associated with expressed TEs were involved in cancer-related signaling pathways (e.g., MYC activity). We identified 264,252 TEs as putative cis-regulatory elements associated with oncogenic pathways such as inflammatory response. We analyzed alterations in TE expression in tumors and their associations with clinical relevance and responses to more than 1000 anticancer drugs. Last, we developed the Atlas of Transposon Expression in Cancer (ATEC), a TE data portal enabling users to explore TE expression patterns, putative regulatory networks, and clinical significance. Overall, this study established a comprehensive resource for TEs across cancer types.

title: Deep hydrous melting of the mantle wedge recorded by Mg isotopes
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Subduction zones govern Earth’s deep volatile cycle. The slab-mantle interface is a key locus of volatile exchange between the subducting crust and the overlying mantle wedge, yet whether and how chemical reactions at this interface affect arc magmatism remains poorly constrained. Arc magmas typically lack a geochemical hallmark of garnet fractionation, leading to the prevailing interpretation that they derive predominantly from the shallower, garnet-free mantle wedge. Here, we challenge this view using Mg isotopic data from Nicaragua, the South Sandwich Islands, and the central-eastern Aleutian arc, integrated with a global arc magma compilation. We show that heavy Mg isotopic signatures in mafic arc magmas vary with indicators of volatile enrichment, pointing to a volatile-rich source, most likely the heavily metasomatized base of the mantle wedge. The heaviest Mg isotopic compositions occur in arcs underlain by the most steeply dipping subducting slab, suggesting a focusing effect by the geometry of the downgoing slab. Monte Carlo isotope mixing models indicate that up to 50% of the Mg budget in some arc magma sources derives from deep, water-saturated melting near the slab-mantle interface. These findings highlight the base of the mantle wedge as a volumetrically and geochemically significant contributor to arc magmatism and the water cycle.

title: Seabirds and native vegetation drive ecosystem processes that support atoll island resilience
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Ecosystem restoration is expected to enhance ecosystem resilience to climate change, but few empirical and mechanistic demonstrations of such assertions exist. Here, we explore this topic for tropical atoll systems, combining science on nutrient subsidies and geo-ecological functions through a unifying ecological energetics lens. We show that native forest cover and seabird nutrient inputs increase primary productivity and secondary metabolism on islands and adjacent coral reefs, scaling with key ecosystem processes. We then demonstrate that seabird and native forest restoration could contribute to reducing island climate change vulnerability by (i) increasing reef accretion rates such that they keep pace with sea-level rise under a 2.0°C warming scenario, (ii) enhancing the production rate of sediment, which could contribute to island maintenance, and (iii) increasing vegetation fine root length, aiding island sediment stabilization. Collectively, our findings provide an integrated energetics and geo-ecological perspective that suggests rewilding of atolls can contribute to climate resilience.

title: Divergent demographic responses to the Kikai-Akahoya volcanic catastrophe in mid-Holocene Japan
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: We examine human demographic responses to one of the Holocene’s largest volcanic eruptions, which devastated East Asia 7300 years ago. Archaeologists have intensively debated the impacts of massive environmental shocks, highlighting either societal collapse or cultural continuity, although few studies situate such catastrophic events within longer-term demographic trajectories. We address this gap in knowledge by using statistical models to infer the demographic and environmental impacts of the Kikai-Akahoya (K-Ah) eruption on Jomon foraging communities occupying the Japanese archipelago. Traditionally framed as an apocalyptic “forcing” mechanism that changed the direction of Japanese prehistory, our results identify a more complex and contingent suite of demographic outcomes. Although we do find evidence of major population collapse in immediately adjacent regions to the volcano, some proximal populations actually increased after the catastrophe, whereas some distal communities were affected by environmental consequences that have hitherto been overlooked. Demographic perspectives on ancient disasters are useful in generating a deeper understanding of the contingent ways in which cultures and societies cope with sudden shocks and catastrophes.

title: Ice nucleation by kaolinite: Morphology shapes the size dependence of ice nucleation active sites on dust particles
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Mineral dusts are the most important type of ice-nucleating particles and play a key role in cloud formation and climate. Their activity is commonly assumed to scale with particle surface area, yet whether this assumption holds across particle sizes remains unverified. Here, we quantify size-dependent ice nucleation activity using compositionally pure, size-segregated kaolinite (KGa-1b). Ice nucleation active site (INAS) densities were determined for size classes from submicron to 48 μm, revealing two distinct ice-nucleation regimes. At low temperatures (∼240 K), INAS density per surface area is independent of particle size. In contrast, at warm temperatures (∼260 K), particles of 6 to 12 μm exhibit the highest INAS densities, up to two orders of magnitude greater than smaller particles and nonsize-selected bulk samples. Linking these results to particle morphology indicates that well-aligned, multilayered platelet edges provide the continuous hydroxylated surfaces required for efficient ice nucleation. Our findings demonstrate that morphology can modulate particle size–dependent ice nucleation, highlighting limitations of simple surface area–based parameterizations.

title: Learning to infer transitively on a mental line in premotor cortex
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Transitive inference (TI) is a form of deductive reasoning that enables the derivation of unknown relationships among premises. It is hypothesized that this cognitive process relies on mapping stimuli onto a “mental line,” a linear workspace organized by arbitrarily assigned ranks. However, its neural basis remains unclear: Does this mental line have a neural correlate and how is it learned? This study investigates the role of dorsal premotor cortex (PMd) in encoding the hypothesized mental line as monkeys acquire item relationships for motor decisions. Findings reveal that PMd multiunit activity organizes along a theoretically predicted direction, supporting a geometrical model that explains behavior. Moreover, a learning process is observed, where the mental line rotates to align with motor planning.

title: Polyclonal breast milk–derived secretory IgA confers broad antiviral protection against multiple respiratory viruses
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Passive immunization is an important tool for protecting individuals with primary immune deficiencies from infectious diseases and offers a rapid response strategy for protecting vulnerable populations, particularly during the interval between pathogen emergence and vaccine deployment. Current approaches rely on intravenous delivery of IgG-enriched plasma or monoclonal antibodies, which limits accessibility, scalability, and effectiveness at mucosal surfaces, the primary entry point for respiratory viruses. Here, we tested LCTG-001, a polyclonal secretory IgA preparation derived from pooled human breast milk, to address these limitations. LCTG-001 demonstrated broad antiviral activity against clinically relevant respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and influenza A virus. LCTG-001 effectively recognized both group 1 and group 2 influenza A subtypes, including the highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, and engaged nonneutralizing effector mechanisms such as neuraminidase inhibition and neutrophil activation. When administered intranasally, LCTG-001 conferred complete protection against influenza A challenge in both immunocompetent and antibody-deficient murine models, preventing morbidity and mortality through a transient early reduction in viral burden followed by sustained improvements in lung pathology and lung barrier integrity. These findings highlight the potential of breast milk–derived secretory IgA as a scalable, mucosa-targeted passive immunization strategy capable of addressing both endemic and emerging respiratory viral threats.

title: Photomapping electrically coupled networks of the mature thalamus and cortex
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Electrical synapses are expressed ubiquitously across the brain and are crucial components of active neural circuitry and connectomes. Identification of coupled networks in living tissue is limited by technical demands of multiplexed recordings, and no dyes, fluorescent reporters, or genetic labels can now fill the gap. We introduce a novel method of identifying and quantifying electrical synapses, opto-δ
                    L
                    , that combines focal photostimulation of soma-targeted opsins with a spike timing–based computation for the strength of electrical synapses to rapidly measure and map electrically coupled networks in vitro. We leverage opto-δ
                    L
                    to show that coupled networks of the mature thalamic reticular nucleus extend as far as 100 micrometers, synapse promiscuously across genetic subtypes of neurons, and couple one to four neighboring neurons to each recorded hub cell. We applied opto-δ
                    L
                    to cortical networks, where we found that somatostatin neurons were more strongly and prevalently coupled. These results highlight the broad potential of opto-δ
                    L
                    to interrogate the identity and roles of electrical synapses in circuitry, behavior, and cognition.

title: Local control of Cre-regulated genetic modeling in vivo using wireless implantable optoelectronics
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Effective modeling of chronic human diseases in vivo requires precise spatiotemporal regulation of molecular processes at defined tissue locations. Optogenetic and optoelectronic tools can provide such control but targeting internal organs such as the lungs remain challenging. To address this, we developed E-LightR-Cre recombinase, enabling precise, spatially restricted gene activation with no dark-state activity and robust blue light responsiveness. To achieve local activation of E-LightR-Cre in specific organ sites, we engineered wireless, fully implantable optoelectronic devices enabling focal illumination of murine lungs with no discernible organ damage. The size of the activated area is controlled by modulating light intensity and duration. Using implanted optoelectronic devices, we activated E-LightR-Cre in a selected area of mouse lungs and achieved local regulation of targeted genes. Light-regulated expression of the oncogenic KRas-G12D mutant in mouse lungs induced local formation of oncogenic lesions. These results show that our protein engineering and adaptable optoelectronic approaches enable facile application of optogenetic tools for locally controlled disease modeling in vivo.

title: Rising global population coexposure to heatwaves and landscape fire-sourced air pollution
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Landscape fires are increasingly threatening public health by causing substantial fire-sourced air pollution (SFAP), with risks amplified during heatwaves. We investigated the global spatial, temporal, and sociodemographic distribution of the population coexposure to heatwaves and SFAP from 2000 to 2019. We found that 52.4% of populated areas and 55.9% of the global population experienced increasing coexposure. On average, 916 million people per year were exposed to at least one coexposure day, increasing by 287 million people per decade. The global annual average exposed days per person was 1.3 days, rising from 1.0 days in 2000–2009 to 1.7 days in 2010–2019. Coexposure person-days increased by 5.5 billion per decade, of which 70.5% was attributable to increasing coexposure intensity and 29.5% to population growth. Countries with a low human development index (HDI) experienced the highest coexposure days per person and the greatest increases. These findings provide high-resolution data to inform health impact assessments and target mitigation and adaptation strategies.

title: SRF3 couples cellular iron homeostasis and defense responses through ubiquitin-dependent nano-organization
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Iron homeostasis is a central component of host defense responses. In mammals, iron availability is rapidly adjusted through receptor mediated pathways, whereas it remains unclear how plants regulate iron homeostasis during the earliest stages of immune activation. Here, we identify a rapid iron regulatory mechanism centered on the plasma membrane receptor kinase STRUBBELIG RECEPTOR FAMILY 3 (SRF3), which integrates bacterial immune signaling with ferrous iron homeostasis. Perception of flagellin triggers a burst of reactive oxygen species that induces a rapid and transient depletion of the labile ferrous iron pool. This state promotes SRF3 ubiquitination and clathrin-dependent endocytosis, a process required to restore intracellular ferrous iron levels while dampening immune responses. Using super resolution microscopy, we show that this functional integration relies on ubiquitin dependent nano organization of SRF3 at the plasma membrane, enabling distinct signaling outputs from a single receptor. Thereby, SRF3 modulates both immune signaling and the proliferation of commensal and pathogenic bacteria.
